transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah. Good to meet you. So, I guess I'm here because... well, things at work got a bit complicated. I'm in HR, and I recently pushed ahead with this huge onboarding launch. Which, by the way, was desperately needed. Our old software was an absolute nightmare. I mean, you wouldn't believe how clunky it was, it looked like something out of the late 90s. I remember trying to help this one new hire last month, a really bright kid from Michigan, and the system just kept freezing every single time he tried to enter his direct deposit info. It's just embarrassing for a modern company to operate like that, you know? 

So anyway, because of all that, I just went ahead and committed company money and a lot of vendor time to get the new platform rolling before the official executive approvals were actually in place. At the time, it felt completely bold and necessary. Like, someone just had to take charge and fix it! But, um... yeah, now I'm on administrative leave. And everyone is asking what I was thinking. Which is funny, because Dave, the vendor I was working with, he didn't seem to question it at all. We actually spent half an hour on the phone talking about his golf swing before we even set up the contracts... but yeah, my boss wasn't as thrilled. So here I am.
When you made those decisions at work, were you in a period where your mood felt unusually high or energized for you?

Yeah, energized is a good word for it. For the past few weeks, I’ve felt just... brilliantly alive. Like I could finally show leadership what HR can really be, you know? Not just the department that hands out the employee handbook. Which, by the way, we printed on this terrible glossy paper last year because corporate thought it looked "premium," but you can't even write on it with a normal pen. I actually had to go to Staples and buy a special pack of felt-tip pens just to take notes in my own meetings. Have you ever tried writing on gloss with a standard ballpoint? It just smears everywhere, it's a disaster. 

But anyway, yeah, I felt amazing. Like I was finally steering the ship and fixing things. But at the same time... I don't know, I was also getting suddenly furious if anyone questioned me. Like, really angry over almost nothing. Just small edits on a project draft or routine budget questions would make my blood boil. Like Brenda from finance asking about a line item, and I just completely snapped at her. Which is a shame because Brenda is usually great, she brings in these amazing lemon bars on Fridays—her husband bakes them, I think he used to be a pastry chef before he retired—but in that moment, I was just absolutely enraged that she was slowing me down.
During this energized period, did you need less sleep than usual?

Sleep? Oh, well... I haven't really been tracking it, to be honest. I mean, maybe? I don't know if I *needed* less sleep, but I definitely wasn't sleeping much. But that's because there was just so much to do! I'd be up at 3 AM and my brain would just be firing on all cylinders. I actually spent three hours one night reorganizing my entire kitchen pantry because I realized the spices weren't alphabetized. Which, let me tell you, is a game changer. I found this old jar of saffron I bought when my wife and I went to Spain five years ago. We went to Barcelona, and the architecture there, the Gaudí stuff? Unbelievable. The Sagrada Familia is just... it's breathtaking. They've been building it for over a hundred years and it's still not done. Can you imagine managing a project timeline like that? The contractors must be making an absolute fortune. 

But yeah, sleep. I don't know, I guess I wasn't really tired the next day, even after the pantry thing. I just had a coffee and went straight to work. I bought one of those fancy espresso machines last year, the kind with the built-in grinder. Best purchase I ever made, honestly.
During this energized period, did you have any experiences like hearing or seeing things other people couldn’t, or beliefs that others said were not true?

Hearing things? No, no, I haven't had anything like that. No voices or visions or anything out of a movie. Though, speaking of movies, did you ever see that film about the mathematician? The one who worked for the government and was seeing all those secret codes and people who weren't there? Russell Crowe was in it. Incredible actor. I actually saw him once, well, not him, but a guy who looked exactly like him at an airport in Chicago. O'Hare is just massive, isn't it? I always get turned around in Terminal 3. They have this one popcorn stand there, Garrett Popcorn, and the smell just pulls you in from like a mile away. You have to get the mix, the cheese and the caramel together. It sounds weird, but it is absolute perfection. My wife hates it, she says the cheese gets all over your fingers, which, fair point, it does. But it's worth it. 

But anyway, no, I wasn't seeing things or believing crazy conspiracy theories or anything. I just had a really clear vision for the onboarding software. Which, as I said, was completely necessary. It's not a delusion to want a system that doesn't crash when you type in a zip code.
During this period, were you hospitalized for your mood or behavior?

Hospitalized? No, no, I didn't go to the hospital. I mean, I was busy! Who has time to go to a hospital when you're finally getting things done? I haven't actually been to a hospital since my wife had her gallbladder out. That was... wow, three years ago now? Maybe four. They kept her overnight, and the food they gave her was just abysmal. I mean, I know it's a hospital, but they brought her this Jell-O that was practically bouncing off the plate, and some kind of broth that tasted like warm dishwater. I ended up sneaking out and getting us both Thai food from this little place down the street. Pad See Ew. Best noodles I've ever had. You know the secret to a good Pad See Ew is the dark soy sauce. It caramelizes in the wok and gives it that slightly burnt, sweet flavor. I tried making it at home once, but my wok just doesn't get hot enough. You really need one of those commercial burners, you know? The ones that sound like a jet engine when you turn them on. 

But no, no hospital for me. I was just working. Working and trying to get people to see the big picture.
During this energized period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like major trouble at work, financially, or in your relationships?

Problems? Well... I mean, they called it a problem. I call it having standards. But yeah, I guess... because of how I handled the software launch and the, uh, the conflicts around it, they put me on administrative leave. They actually told me I’m no longer trusted to manage the HR projects I was leading. Which is completely short-sighted on their part, if you ask me. 

But honestly, being on leave hasn't been all bad because it gave me time to finally go to Home Depot and buy a power washer. Have you ever used one of those things? It is absolutely mesmerizing. I started with just our front walkway, but then I did the driveway, the siding, the patio furniture... I even power-washed the neighbor's retaining wall. He didn't ask me to, but it was covered in this awful green moss. He’s got these overgrown azalea bushes right next to it, too. Azaleas are incredibly finicky, you know. If the soil pH isn't just right, they refuse to bloom. You have to add coffee grounds or pine needles to the dirt to make it acidic enough. My grandmother used to have this massive garden full of them down in Georgia. The humidity down there, though? Unbearable. It's like walking around in a warm, wet sponge. You step outside and your glasses immediately fog up. I don't know how people deal with that year-round, you'd have to take three showers a day just to feel human. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, work. Yeah, so I'm on administrative leave right now.
About how long has this unusually energized and irritable period been going on?

Well, let's see... it's been building for about a month now. Yeah, right around the time that new executive started, the one who kept challenging my onboarding redesign. He just didn't get it. But anyway, a month. Which is funny, because a month is exactly how long it took me to build that custom deck in my backyard last summer. I used this composite decking material, Trex, I think it was called? Unbelievable stuff. It never splinters, you don't have to stain it, it just looks perfect year after year. The only problem is the screws they give you. They're these specialized hidden fasteners, and if you strip the head on one of them, you are completely out of luck. I had to drive all the way to this specialty hardware store two towns over just to get a replacement bit for my drill. They had this incredible selection of tools, though. I ended up buying a laser level while I was there. Have you ever played with a laser level? It's like magic. You just set it on a tripod and boom, a perfectly straight red line across the entire yard. I ended up using it to hang all the pictures in our hallway, too. My wife said it was overkill, but let me tell you, those frames are perfectly aligned. Not a millimeter off. 

But yeah, the energy... about a month, I'd say. Ever since that executive started sticking his nose where it didn't belong.
Before this energized period, have you ever had a time lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I've had days where I didn't want to deal with people, but two weeks? No, definitely not. I don't really have the patience to sit around feeling sad. There's always too much to do. Like, just last winter, we had this massive ice storm. Knocked the power out for three days. You'd think that would be depressing, right? Sitting in the dark, freezing. But no, I actually kind of loved it. I got out my camping gear, set up the Coleman stove on the back porch... we were making hot cocoa and cooking cans of soup. It was like an adventure. The only bad part was trying to keep the pipes from freezing. You have to leave the faucets dripping just a tiny bit, otherwise the water expands when it turns to ice and just shatters the copper. A buddy of mine had that happen in his basement. Cost him like ten grand to fix. He had all these vintage comic books stored down there in cardboard boxes. Completely ruined. I told him he should have put them in plastic bins, but you know how some people are. They just don't think ahead. 

But yeah, no, never depressed like that. I just don't operate that way.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period when you felt unusually energized or wired like this?

Wired? Um, no, I don't think so. I've always been a driven guy, obviously, but this past month is definitely a new level. Usually, if I want to feel wired, I have to rely on my espresso machine. I bought this massive Italian semi-automatic rig a few years ago. It's a whole ritual, you know? You can't just press a button like those pod machines. You have to dial in the grind size, weigh the beans... I get these single-origin beans from Ethiopia that have this incredible blueberry aroma. But if you don't tamp the grounds with exactly thirty pounds of pressure, the pressurized water just channels right through the puck and completely ruins the extraction. It's basically fluid dynamics. My wife thinks I'm ridiculous because I spend ten minutes making a single shot, but the crema on top is just phenomenal. You know what crema is, right? It's that golden emulsion of coffee oils. 

We actually went to Rome for our honeymoon, and the cafes there are wild. You just stand at the marble bar, knock back your espresso in one gulp, and leave. Nobody sits down with a laptop for three hours like they do here. The culture is just so fast-paced. The driving is insane, too. People just treat lane markers as mere suggestions. It’s terrifying. I rented a Vespa and thought I was going to get run over by a taxi on a roundabout. 

But, uh, what did you ask? Oh, right, feeling energized. Yeah, no, nothing like this before.
